exposure: Socio-demographic factors (urban residency, high caste, advanced age)
Health service-related factors (e.g., lack of resources, awareness, appropriate policies)
cohort: The study analyzed 661 birth records from two urban hospitals in Kathmandu for the fiscal year 2018/19 and included interviews with health professionals and pregnant women.
finding: The overall Caesarean section rate was high at 50.2%, with private hospitals having nearly double the rate of public hospitals, and previous Caesarean section being the leading indication.
mod_finding: Factors significantly associated with higher odds of Caesarean section included private hospital setting, maternal age 25 years and above, four or more antenatal visits, breech presentation, urban residency, high caste, gestational age 37-40 weeks, spontaneous labour or no labour, and previous Caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collection occurred in 2021, utilizing birth records from the fiscal year 2018/19.
gest_age: Gestational age between 37-40 weeks was identified as a factor associated with higher CS rates.
